hero.subtitle: When a diagnosis or treatment goes wrong at a Siskiyou County clinic or hospital, the aftermath can feel isolating in a small mountain town like Mount Shasta. We can help you understand your options under California's medical malpractice rules and review what happened at no cost.

about.title: Mount Shasta Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Mount Shasta residents rely on a small circle of local clinics and the nearest regional hospitals for care, and when something goes wrong during treatment, patients often aren't sure where to turn. Medical malpractice covers situations where a provider's care fell below the accepted standard and caused harm — not simply a case where treatment didn't work out as hoped. California law places specific limits on these claims, including strict notice periods and a requirement for qualified medical expert review before a case can move forward. Because Mount Shasta's population is small and healthcare options are limited, gathering records and expert opinions can take extra coordination. We handle medical malpractice claims directly and can review what happened and explain your options under California's malpractice statutes.

items.title: Strict Timelines Matter
items.desc: California generally requires malpractice claims to be filed within one year of discovering the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself. We can help you understand how these deadlines apply before time runs out.

items.title: Pre-Suit Notice Is Required
items.desc: California law requires a 90-day notice to the provider before a lawsuit can be filed. Our team can help make sure this step is handled correctly so your claim isn't delayed or dismissed on a technicality.

items.title: Expert Review Is Usually Necessary
items.desc: Because a bad medical outcome alone doesn't prove malpractice, California cases almost always require a qualified medical expert to establish that the standard of care was breached. Reaching out early helps get this process started.

items.question: How long do I have to file a medical malpractice claim in Mount Shasta?
items.answer: Under California's MICRA rules, you generally have one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, and no more than three years from the date the injury occurred. These deadlines can be affected by other factors, so it's worth having our team review your specific timeline. Missing the window can mean losing the right to file at all.

items.question: Is a bad medical outcome automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law recognizes that not every poor result from treatment means a provider was negligent. To have a valid claim, the care given generally must have fallen below the accepted medical standard, and that failure must have caused the harm. A qualified medical expert typically needs to confirm this before a case can proceed.

items.question: My provider is in a small network around Mount Shasta — does that change anything?
items.answer: Mount Shasta's limited number of local clinics and providers doesn't change the underlying California malpractice rules, but it can affect how records are gathered and which experts are available to review your case. Our team is familiar with rural Siskiyou County healthcare access and can help navigate those practical steps.
